articleTitle: A Study of 3D Point Cloud Feature Extraction Method Based on Multi-Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: To address the sparsity and irregularity of 3D point cloud data and enhance feature extraction through multi-feature fusion, this paper proposes the Multi-Feature Fusion Point Cloud Network (MFF-PCN). The network computes hybrid features from each point's spatial coordinates and geometric attributes using a Local Spatial Geometry Information Encoding Module and an FPFH-based Feature Extraction Module. The local encoding module captures geometric relationships by encoding self-coordinates, relative coordinates, and point-pair features (PPF), while the FPFH module further refines local features with Simplified Point Feature Histograms (SPFH) and weighted neighbor combinations. Experiments show a classification accuracy of 91.3% and overall accuracy of 93.3% on the ModelNet40 dataset.

articleTitle: DA-SlowFast Network for Abnormal Action Detection in the Workshop
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: The detection of abnormal workshop actions plays a vital role in industrial production, which gives timely warning when the workshop employees behave abnormally and thus greatly reduce the probability of workshop safety accidents. Despite the tremendous advances in action recognition and detection technology in recent years, real-time abnormal action detection remains a challenging task due to the complexity of video data and the huge computational costs. In order to achieve high accuracy detection of abnormal actions in complex workshop scenarios, this paper proposes a DA-SlowFast algorithm for workshop abnormal action detection. The algorithm can be used to detect six common types of abnormal actions in the workshop (talking on the phone, sleeping on the workbench, falling, running violently, fighting, playing with cell phones). Based on the original SlowFast network, we incorporate the hybrid domain attention mechanism (DANet) in the Slow branching and lateral connectivity processes, in order to improve the model's detection accuracy for static actions and its ability to capture fine-grained motion details. In addition, for purpose of solving the problem of unbalanced samples of various types of actions in the video dataset, we replace the Cross Entropy Loss function for the action classification task in the original model with the Focal Loss function. The results of the ablation experiments show that the efficient hybrid attention mechanism introduced in the SlowFast model significantly improves the detection accuracy. And the final DA-SlowFast model also obtains the highest detection accuracy compared to other similar models on the workshop dataset.

articleTitle: Investigation of Complex Underwater Environments for Target Recognition Based on Improved YOLOv7-Tiny
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: The sustainable utilization of marine biological resources requires long-term monitoring of underwater ecosystems, yet traditional detection methods often rely on manual labor and fall short. This study addresses underwater target detection in complex environments, using scallop recognition as a case study, and proposes an improved YOLOv7-tiny algorithm. First, the Coordinate Attention (CA) mechanism is integrated into the neck component, resulting in a Coordinate Attention Convolution (CAConv) that enhances model performance. Second, the Feature Pyramid Network (FPN) structure is strengthened to improve detection across various scales. Finally, the EIoU loss function is incorporated to boost accuracy and robustness. Compared to similar detection models, the proposed algorithm shows significant improvements in average precision and recall rate.

articleTitle: Design Study on Hierarchical Analysis Based and Dynamic Information Visualisation Gene of Endangered Plants - A Case Study of South China Botanical Garden
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Digital technology has fast and convenient advantages and broad application prospects in information dissemination, and combining it with plant information visualisation is conducive to the promotion of information popularisation and protection of endangered plants. This paper uses the hierarchical analysis method to take endangered aquatic plants in South China Botanical Garden as the research object, constructs the information model, and completes the information visualisation design design with more intuitive and novel dynamic effects, and promotes its information dissemination with digital empowerment to achieve the effect of improving the popularisation of endangered plants and people's awareness of protection.

articleTitle: Visualization of Hotspots and Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence in Education - Based on Citespace Knowledge Map Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the advent of the digital age, the deep integration of artificial intelligence and education has attracted extensive attention in the academic community. In this study, 1,193 literatures directly related to AI education in the Web of Science core database in the past ten years were knowledge mapped and visualized with the help of CiteSpace software. Through the analysis of co-occurrence, clustering, and emergence of the literature data, it is found that the number of related literature issued in 2014–2014 increased significantly, with a certain degree of aggregation and depth. It also shows the hotspots and cutting-edge trends of artificial intelligence education research. The research hotspots are mainly centered on artificial intelligence, digital education, recognition, school, identification, educational data mining, human-computer interaction, etc., but the research method is relatively single, the authors and the interdisciplinary cooperation between institutions is not close enough, and there is a problem of bias in the region of research institutions. Future research can try to strengthen interdisciplinary cooperation, innovate institutional cooperation modes, and establish visualization standards, so as to stimulate the endogenous momentum of the deep integration of AI and education.

articleTitle: Research on 3D Visualization Modeling of Bridge Real Scene Based on OpenGL Graphics Library and Image Sequence
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In order to more accurately analyze the actual state of the bridge, building an accurate model is one of the effective technical means. For this reason, this paper puts forward the research on three-dimensional visual modeling of bridge reality based on OpenGL graphics library and image sequence. After defining the relationship between the bridge images taken continuously by using the homography matrix, the bridge image sequences are sorted; The Marching Cubes algorithm in OpenGL is used to reconstruct the Poisson surface, determine the smooth 3D mesh of the bridge model, render it, and output the 3D visualization model of the real bridge. In the test results, the output model can accurately feedback the actual situation of each component of the bridge.

articleTitle: Distributed Dynamic Event-Triggered Consensus for Linear Multi-Agent Systems with Bounded Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In this paper, the consensus of general multi-agent systems under bounded disturbance is studied based on the event triggering control method of relative state information state estimation. The method is more flexible by adding a state-related item to the design of trigger threshold. Firstly, the fully distributed event-triggered protocol can satisfy the sufficient condition of consensus by using algebraic graph theory and Lyapunov theory. Secondly, the protocol can obtain that the adjacent trigger interval is strictly greater than zero, thus excluding Zeno behavior. Finally, the effectiveness of the protocol under bounded interference can be verified by experimental simulation.

articleTitle: DFSMDA: A Domain Adaptation Algorithm with Domain Feature Extraction for EEG Emotion Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In the realm of EEG-based emotion recognition, individual differences present significant challenges for cross-subject recognition, making it an essential area of research. While many existing methods utilize unsupervised multi-source domain adaptation techniques to mitigate these differences, they often fall short in achieving effective recognition performance. To alleviate this issue, this paper introduces a domain feature-aware semi-supervised multi-source domain adaptation emotion recognition model, named DFSMDA. The proposed approach employs a multi-branch network to extract both domain-invariant and domain-specific features while applying domain adaptation methods to minimize distribution discrepancies between source and target domains. Additionally, during training, we utilize a limited number of labeled samples from the target domain to enhance model suitability for recognition tasks. We validated the model through cross-subject emotion recognition experiments on the publicly available SEED dataset. The results demonstrate that our method achieves outstanding performance, with an average recognition accuracy of 92.76% across three sessions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Equipment Application Research and Analysis Based on AR Interactive Mode
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Driven by advances in automated production equipment and digital technology, the development of intelligent equipment is progressing rapidly. Augmented Reality (AR) technology, which integrates reality and virtual environments to provide an immersive experience, is being increasingly applied to intelligent equipment. Many researchers have conducted in-depth explorations of this technology. In line with the evolving needs of intelligent equipment, this paper presents research and analysis on the application of AR in interactive systems for intelligent equipment. First, the display principles of the AR interactive system are thoroughly analyzed, designed, and tested on a robotic arm. Then, in response to the actual needs of an intelligent factory, the corrosion of the connectors in skid-mounted equipment is used as a case study to design a finite element model. This analysis model is deployed on a server and accessed via the AR interactive system to derive conclusions. Experimental testing and user experience demonstrate that AR technology significantly enhances the intelligence and digitalization of automated equipment while offering a novel working experience.

articleTitle: A Knowledge Fusion Learning Method for Reinforcement Learning in Different Tasks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In order to improve the learning efficiency of reinforcement learning agents on new tasks, this paper designs a knowledge fusion learning method, enabling agents to acquire knowledge from multiple old tasks. First, the architecture of the knowledge fusion learning algorithm is constructed; Second, information that can represent task characteristics is analyzed; Finally, an algorithm is designed to project the feature information of old and new tasks to form knowledge. Simulation experiments show that the knowledge fusion learning method allows new agents to learn new tasks by utilizing information from multiple less-related source tasks.

articleTitle: Depth Completion of Transparent Objects Based on Feature Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Accurately perceiving the depth of transparent objects is crucial for modern automation and robotics but is challenging due to their optical properties. To address this challenge, This paper proposes an MFAU-Net-based depth completion method for transparent objects, utilizing geometric features from RGB images and introducing the Encoder Attention Module (EAM) and Feature Fusion Module (FFM) for effective multi-level feature extraction and fusion. Compared to the ClearGrasp model, the RMSE improves by 15.97% and the MAE by 14.81%. Experimental results show that MFAU-Net significantly enhances depth estimation precision and resilience, providing a novel approach for transparent object depth perception.

articleTitle: 2D LiDAR Point Cloud Correction Method for Spherical Robot
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: To address the distortion of point cloud data caused by the pitch angle oscillation of the LiDAR during the motion of a spherical robot, this study proposes a correction method for LiDAR point cloud data based on IMU. The proposed method achieves time synchronization between IMU and LiDAR data through spherical linear interpolation. A composite criterion combines point cloud distance differences with the LiDAR pitch angle to identify outlier point cloud data. Based on this, a linear regression model is employed to predict and correct these outliers, and coordinate transformations are applied to adjust the pitch angle of the point cloud data, resulting in corrected LiDAR point cloud data that more closely approximates the true values. A spherical robot simulation model was constructed based on Gazebo, and the simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces the error in LiDAR point cloud data and enhances the environmental detection accuracy of the spherical robot.

articleTitle: AAKA-WCS: Anonymous Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for Wearable Computing Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the development of Internet of Things (IoT) technology, various wearable devices such as smartwatches and fitness trackers have integrated into our daily lives. However, due to their limited computational resources, traditional security mechanisms are not suitable for these wearable devices. Consequently, ensuring efficient and secure authentication and key agreement while protecting user privacy to prevent unauthorized data access and tampering has become a pressing issue. In this paper, we propose an Anonymous Authentication and Key Agreement Protocol for Wearable Computing Scenarios (AAKA-WCS) based on the lightweight authenticated encryption algorithm AEGIS. This protocol is specifically designed to address the challenges of secure and efficient authentication and key agreement among various entities in wearable computing scenarios. Comprehensive security functionality comparisons and performance evaluations with existing protocols demonstrate that AAKA-WCS provides sufficient security features while maintaining low system overhead, making it more suitable for resource-constrained wearable computing environments.

articleTitle: Safety-Aware Path Planning for Post-Disaster Rescue Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Emergency rescue vehicles play a vital role in dealing with traffic accidents and emergencies. Emergency rescue vehicles can reduce accident losses by arriving at the accident site in time. Reasonable planning of emergency vehicle routes can shorten the travel time of the route and improve the safety of the route. However, due to the dynamic and changeable actual road network environment and various uncertainties, congestion or accidents may occur at any time, resulting in low rescue efficiency and high risk of rescue routes. In response to the above problems, this thesis proposes a global path planning algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning. In response to complex and changeable road conditions, this thesis adds a path situation awareness module to the global path planning algorithm based on DQN, and proposes a Transformer-based prediction algorithm to perceive road condition changes, adjust the global path in real time, avoid congested paths and risky paths, improve the rescue efficiency of emergency rescue vehicles, and ensure driving safety. According to different evaluation indicators, this thesis conducts simulation experiments on the global path planning algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning. The experimental results show that the route travel time planned by the proposed algorithm is lower than that of the benchmark algorithm, the safety is higher than that of the benchmark algorithm, and the success rate of pathfinding has improved by 14% compared to the baseline algorithms.

articleTitle: Forecasting Road Crash Trend Utilizing Recurrent Neural Network: A Time Series Analysis Approach in the City of Manila
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Urban areas face significant challenges in achieving sustainable development, with road safety being a critical aspect of urban sustainability. In the City of Manila, there are a lot of factors that contribute to road crashes and road accidents, posing risks to all road users including drivers, commuters, and pedestrians. This research proposes a solution leveraging the Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) for predicting road crashes depending on the time and location where the road crash occurred. By analyzing historical road crash data alongside various parameters, such as the date and location of the crash, the RNN model aims to forecast potential accident hotspots. Through this predictive approach, urban planners and policymakers can proactively address road safety concerns by prioritizing developing and maintaining traffic control infrastructure and policies that will lessen road crashes. The findings of this study offer valuable insights into enhancing sustainable cities and communities by mitigating road accidents through data-driven interventions and modernization efforts in traffic management systems. The findings of the study can also contribute to fostering innovation through integrating advanced technologies such as recurrent neural networks in infrastructure planning and management industries.

articleTitle: A System Design for Virtual Reality Visualization of Hydrological and Meteorological Data
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: The study introduces a tailored virtual reality (VR) visualization system designed for the analysis and monitoring of hydrological and meteorological data, with a specific focus on the Yellow River basin in China. Utilizing Unity3D and C#, the system is capable of generating realistic virtual environments and facilitating diverse interactions, such as real-time monitoring, data analysis, and hazard warning functionalities. Users have the ability to fully immerse themselves in a virtual hydrological station, enabling direct observation of changes in hydrological and meteorological data while interacting with the environment through VR devices. Furthermore, an integral cultural hall within the system serves to exhibit the rich history and culture of the Yellow River, thereby enhancing its cultural significance. This innovative system not only enhances efficiency in hydrological monitoring but also contributes to raising public awareness regarding river management. The research underscores the potential applications of VR technology in water resource management, offering valuable insights for similar systems development across various regions.

articleTitle: Ground Penetrating Radar Signal Denoising Based on Multi-Scale Feature Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the rapid development of electronic information technology, Ground Penetrating Radar (GPR) technology has become an indispensable tool in fields such as urban construction, archaeology, and the military. However, due to the heterogeneity of underground media, scattering of electromagnetic waves, and equipment errors, GPR signals are often disturbed by noise, affecting detection accuracy. Therefore, this paper designs a multi-scale feature fusion network to enhance the robustness of denoising models for denoising GPR signals with different characteristics. The network is constructed based on the Inception architecture and consists of three parts: an encoder structure for extracting multi-scale features of GPR signals, a disentangler structure for classifying data features and generating corresponding feature masks, and a decoder for reconstructing the denoised signal. Additionally, ID-Net can also extract noise features, enhancing the model's interpretability. Experiments have proven that ID-Net outperforms traditional denoising models in removing GPR noise and demonstrates good denoising capabilities on datasets with different characteristics, proving the robustness of ID-Net in denoising GPR noise signals with different features.

articleTitle: Optimized Particle Swarm-Ant Colony Fusion for UAV Path Planning Research
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Ant Colony Algorithm (ACO) and Particle Swarm Algorithm (PSO) are two heuristic algorithms commonly used in three-dimensional path planning for UAVs. The particle swarm algorithm is prone to produce local optimization, while the ACO algorithm has a slow convergence speed. Therefore, a new fusion algorithm is proposed to address the above problems. The fusion algorithm utilizes the early and fast convergence of the particle swarm algorithm to generate a suboptimal solution as the initial condition of the pheromone distribution of the ant colony algorithm, and then fuses the two improved algorithms to obtain the final path planning scheme. Experimental results show that this fusion algorithm outperforms the other three algorithms in terms of convergence speed and convergence accuracy.

articleTitle: DyFormer: A CNN-Transformer Network Combining Local and Global Attention for Optical Remote Sensing Object Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Remote sensing image (RSI) object detection is crucial for natural disaster management, urban planning, and resource exploration. However, due to significant differences between RSIs and natural images (NIs), existing object detectors designed for NIs are not directly applicable to RSIs. CNN-based models typically require specialized attention modules to relate small targets to global contexts, while Transformer-based models often add modules to enhance detail extraction, increasing computational costs for edge deployment. To address these challenges, we propose DyFormer, a hybrid CNN-Transformer model that combines local and global attention mechanisms for effective feature fusion. Additionally, a feature residual pyramid network (FRPN) is introduced to enhance multi-scale feature integration. We conduct experiments on the open source NWPU VHR-10 dataset to evaluate the proposed DyFormer, achieving a mAP@0.5 of 61.7%, outperforms existing sort-of-the-art methods, demonstrating its effectiveness for RSI object detection tasks.

articleTitle: Regional Face Recognition Algorithm Based on Ahash and Face Anti-Spoofing Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence technology, facial recognition algorithms have been used in many fields. However, current algorithms still face challenges, including accuracy, real-time performance, etc. This article presents a regional face recognition algorithm to improve the accuracy of facial recognition. The method first compares the information of different users with existing data in the database. It categorizes users into different regions and assigns specific actions for users in those regions. Comparing the accuracy of this method with other facial recognition approaches shows its effectiveness in enhancing accuracy. This also provides new insights for the future development of facial recognition technology.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Target Damage Effect Based on LiDAR
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In order to achieve rapid and accurate damage effect evaluation on the target through unmanned damage effect testing, a study on the vulnerability of combat targets is conduct for the military's fourth-generation fighter F-22 of US. Based on the analysis of the structure and function of the F-22, the aircraft body structure damage tree is established. The point cloud model of the aircraft body before and after the attack is established by the laser radar carried by the UAV. The quantification of the damage effect on the fighter, resulting from the shock wave overpressure damage element, has been conducted. By integrating and optimizing the ICP algorithm, the problem of aircraft body alignment before and after the attack is solved, and rapid damage effect assessment of the F-22 under the shock wave overpressure is achieved.

articleTitle: The Position Visualization Modeling of Mechanical Product Assembly Line Based on Equidistant Helix
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: This study presents a uniformly spaced recursive model to determine the position and velocity magnitude of mechanical products at various locations and time intervals. By assuming a constant speed for the assembly line, the position of the initial product at different time intervals is calculated using arc length. Building upon this, a node position model based on the Cosine Rule is applied to recursively determine the front handle center of each subsequent product relative to the rear handle center of the preceding product. To account for the assembly line's exit, a “turning area” with a 2:1 circular arc ratio centered around the center point is introduced. MATLAB coding is utilized to visualize and establish the model.

articleTitle: An Immersive Ceramic Display and Personalized Decoration Method Based on WebVR
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the advent of the digital age, virtual ceramic display platforms have emerged, utilizing virtual reality technology to break geographical boundaries, allowing ceramic enthusiasts from around the world to appreciate and explore the art of ceramics in an immersive environment. Existing virtual display platforms are primarily limited to applying texture maps on preset blank ceramic models, lacking simulation of the diversity and complexity of real ceramics. This paper proposes a virtual display and decoration method for ceramic products based on WebVR, featuring two major functions: virtual display of ceramic products and virtual decoration. Through the method of updating decorative textures of ceramic products, it realizes virtual decoration based on the virtual display of ceramic products, which not only breaks the spatial and temporal limitations of ceramic product display and compensates for the fragility of ceramic products, but also provides users with a highly personalized experience, offering ceramic enthusiasts an information-based solution to truly feel the charm of ceramic art in a virtual environment.

articleTitle: Classification Methoed of Cement Concrete Pavement Conditions Based on Improved EfficientNet
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Given the drawback of high complexity and low recognition rate of the existing cement concrete pavement state classification models and methods, this paper proposes an improved model based on EfficientNet for the classification of cement concrete pavement states in five cases. A more comprehensive and effective feature extraction ability for the model is provided by an attention module for the performance of convolutional neural networks introduced in the model. To reduce the model complexity, an efficient channel attention module is introduced. The improved network model has higher detection accuracy and better adapts to the classification of cement concrete pavement states. The image samples come from the open-source dataset (Road Surface Classification Dataset, RSCD). Through reclassification, a total of 58,568 images of five types of cement concrete pavements in different weather conditions are established as the dataset to train the proposed model and obtain the classification results of cement concrete pavement images. The experimental results show that the accuracy of the proposed model on the dataset reaches 95.57%, which is better than other comparison models and can accurately and effectively classify the cement concrete pavement states under different conditions.

articleTitle: An Intelligent Collaborative Decision-Making Method for Multi-Target Tracking in Heterogeneous Unmanned Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and robotics, unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) swarm systems have received widespread attention from domestic and foreign experts, scholars, and research institutions for their applications in military and civilian fields. This research primarily focuses on intelligent collaborative decision-making methods for heterogeneous unmanned swarms in multi-target tracking tasks. In response to the challenges associated with the difficulty of obtaining global states and the complexity of collaborative decision-making in existing methods, a distributed collaborative decision-making strategy based on Multi-Agent Deep Reinforcement Learning (MADRL) has been proposed. This strategy employs a data-driven approach that eliminates the need for precise modeling, utilizing a hierarchical attention mechanism to process heterogeneous information. Additionally, we have designed an experience-sharing training mechanism for heterogeneous swarms to enhance their intelligent collaborative decision-making capabilities and multi-target tracking performance. By establishing a simulation environment, various MADRL algorithms were implemented and experimentally validated. The experimental results show that the proposed method can effectively improve the collaborative tracking performance of UAV swarms. Future work will focus on hyperparameter tuning of algorithms, testing across different swarm scales, and analyzing algorithm scalability in diverse environments.

articleTitle: YOLOv8-FW: Rail Surface Defect Detection Algorithm Integrating Frequency Domain Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Rail defect detection plays a crucial role in preventing train derailments and ensuring passenger safety. However, the continuous operation of trains can lead to the compression and abrasion of rails, resulting in defects such as delamination, subsidence, and scratches, which significantly compromise train safety. To address the limitations of existing detection algorithms in recognizing subsidence and scratch defects, this paper proposes a YOLOv8-FW model that incorporates frequency domain features for automated rail surface defect detection. By introducing the Frequency Domain Attention (FDA) mechanism into the backbone network of YOLOv8, the model can effectively transform spatial domain features into the frequency domain, thereby improving the recognition capability of defects with similar background features, such as subsidence. Additionally, the integration of the Wavelet Hybrid Convolution (WHC) module reduces feature loss and enhances the model's ability to detect small-target defects, such as scratches. Experimental results demonstrate that the YOLOv8-FW model achieves a 3.2% improvement in mean average precision compared to the YOLOv8n model, effectively enhancing the model's detection capabilities for small targets and defects with similar features.

articleTitle: Psychological and Emotional Driven Virtual Reality Human-Computer Interaction Based on Recurrent Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In the field of virtual reality human-computer interaction, traditional interaction methods are difficult to accurately respond to users' emotional states, resulting in a less natural and immersive experience. To address this issue, this article investigates a psychological emotion driven interaction method based on recurrent neural networks (RNN), aiming to enhance the emotion recognition and response capabilities of virtual reality systems. The article collects physiological and behavioral data of users in virtual environments, including heart rate, facial expressions, and movement trajectories; then, an emotion state analysis model is constructed using RNN, and the model parameters are optimized through training the dataset to improve the accuracy of emotion recognition. The experimental results show that the accuracy of this method in identifying psychological emotions reaches 92%, significantly higher than the 78% of traditional methods; meanwhile, user interaction satisfaction increases by 17.7%. The conclusion points out that emotion driven methods based on RNN significantly enhance the naturalness and user experience of virtual reality interaction, providing a new path for the future development of human-computer interaction.

articleTitle: Research on Anomaly Detection Model for Power Industrial Control Networks Based on Bidirectional Recurrent Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In response to the current challenges of low accuracy in detecting abnormal data traffic and insufficient sample space in power industrial control networks, we propose a novel approach. Our method involves leveraging bidirectional recurrent neural networks(Bi-RNN) with long short-term memory (LSTM) architecture for anomaly traffic detection. Additionally, we introduce a sample augmentation technique based on generative adversarial networks (GAN) to address the limited sample size issue. We train our model on training datasets with temporal characteristics and evaluate its performance on testing datasets, achieving a prediction accuracy exceeding 99.6%. Moreover, through the sample augmentation model, we expand the dataset by over 100,000 samples.

articleTitle: The Impact of REM Sleep Fragmentation on Depression: A Cross-Sectional Analysis Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: This study explores the predictive relationship between REM sleep fragmentation and depressive symptoms across a heterogeneous participant sample, including both obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) patients and non-OSA individuals. Previous research has highlighted the impact of REM fragmentation on emotional regulation and its association with increased risks of depression. However, these studies primarily focus on OSA populations, leaving the effects on non-OSA individuals underexplored. This research aims to bridge that gap by evaluating whether REM fragmentation, combined with physiological factors such as neck circumference, BMI, and age, can predict Hospital Anxiety and Depression Scale - Depression Subscale (HADSD) scores. Using machine learning models, including Support Vector Regression (SVR) and K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), we assessed the predictive performance of these variables across 144 polysomnography (PSG) recordings. The results showed that REM fragmentation emerged as the most significant predictor of HADSD scores, with SVR outperforming KNN in terms of overall accuracy and specificity. These findings highlight the importance of REM fragmentation as a critical marker for psychological health risk, extending its relevance beyond OSA populations.

articleTitle: Advancements and Challenges in Virtual Reality: A Comprehensive Overview of Tracking and Display Technologies
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) has evolved significantly from its nascent stages in the mid-20th century to its current state, characterized by sophisticated tracking and display technologies. This manuscript delves into the historical progression of VR, highlighting key milestones and innovations. It provides an in-depth analysis of tracking systems, including wireless tracking, inertial tracking, and sensor fusion, discussing their operational principles, advantages, and limitations. Additionally, the manuscript explores various display technologies such as Liquid Crystal Display (LCD) and Light Emitting Diode (LED) screens, emphasizing their impact on the user experience. Key features affecting VR immersion, including resolution, frame rate, screen curvature, and device weight, are examined. The paper concludes with a discussion on future trends and the potential for specialized VR systems designed to accommodate users with specific needs, such as severe myopia and color blindness.

articleTitle: A Multimodal Virtual Reality System for Switchgear Operation Training: Integration of Dynamic Gesture and Speech Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: This paper introduces a multimodal interaction system for switchgear operation training, utilizing virtual reality (VR) technology combined with gesture recognition and speech recognition techniques. The system provides an immersive training environment designed to improve operational accuracy and user engagement. Dynamic gesture recognition and two speech recognition models—K2 (Next-Gen Kaldi) and GMM-HMM with LSTM—were integrated to facilitate intuitive interactions. Experimental evaluations demonstrated that the system offers significant improvements in task accuracy, user experience, and training efficiency compared to traditional methods. The K2 model outperformed the GMM-HMM with LSTM approach in terms of speech recognition accuracy. Additionally, user feedback confirmed the effectiveness of the multimodal interaction system in simplifying complex operational tasks. Future work will explore the application of large language models to enhance natural language understanding and further refine the system's usability. This study highlights the potential of integrating advanced multimodal technologies into industrial training systems to enhance both safety and proficiency.

articleTitle: A Review of Artificial Intelligence-Enhanced Security Solutions for the Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: The rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) is fundamentally transforming various industries, with many IoT systems increasingly driven by artificial intelligence (AI). Advances in AI introduce new changes and breakthroughs in IoT, while the swift progress of IoT technology also presents significant security and privacy challenges. This paper reviews the major security issues and solutions within AI-driven IoT environments, focusing on key management protocols, intrusion detection systems, physical layer authentication, and data encryption. It examines the advantages and limitations of symmetric and asymmetric key management, the roles of network-based and host-based intrusion detection systems, and how physical layer authentication enhances device security through wireless signal characteristics. Additionally, the paper discusses the role of homomorphic encryption and privacy protection technologies, suggesting that integrating these methods represents an effective strategy for addressing IoT security challenges. Future research directions include developing scalable security protocols, advanced threat detection systems, and incorporating AI to enhance the resilience and efficiency of IoT security measures.

articleTitle: Advancing Spatiotemporal Fusion for Enhanced Perception in Dynamic Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: The increasing demand for robust perception systems in autonomous driving has highlighted the limitations of traditional single-modal approaches, particularly in noisy and dynamic urban environments. This paper introduces the DFBEV framework, which utilizes innovative spatiotemporal sampling and fusion strategies to enhance 3D perception. By integrating multi-frame data, DFBEV effectively captures dynamic changes and maintains target consistency. Key components, such as Pillar queries and an image denoising module, significantly improve detection accuracy and computational efficiency. Despite relying on image data, DFBEV provides a strong foundation for future enhancements, including multimodal sensor integration and vehicle-to-infrastructure (V2I) collaborations. Through comprehensive ablation studies, we demonstrate the framework's potential in transforming next-generation intelligent transportation systems.

articleTitle: Review of VREED in Eye Tracking-Based VR Emotion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Eye-tracking emotion detection, especially within virtual reality (VR) environments, has potential to be a key technology that has implications across various industries. The VREED dataset serves as a baseline for research in emotion classification tasks using eye-tracking, galvanic skin response (GSR), and electrocardiogram (ECG) data. This study expands on the original VREED research by applying 17 different classifiers across six emotion classification tasks. Feature selection is used to address data scarcity and assess the impact of selecting specific features versus utilizing the full feature set. Results showed some promising classifiers, with feature selection further improving performance for certain models. This demonstrates the value of optimizing this feature selection process and suggests further techniques in yielding better results. This study serves as an extension of the baseline of VREED and provides insight into improving the robustness of emotion detection models in VR, with applications in healthcare, education, and gaming.

articleTitle: The Study on Sweetness Enhancement Design in Augmented Reality Based on Synesthesia Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: Taste is influenced by both the food's inherent taste and its visual appearance. Previous research shows stable synesthesia between visual features (e.g., color, shape) and taste perceptions (e.g., sweetness, sourness). However, past studies mostly relied on 2D images and taste-related words, which may limit their practical application. This study uses augmented reality (AR) to overlay virtual 3D dessert images onto real desserts. Participants tasted the virtual desserts and rated their sweetness, liking, and congruency. The findings revealed that desserts with rounded shapes and fewer visual elements were perceived as sweeter than desserts with angular shapes and more elements. Smooth textures also enhanced perceived sweetness compared to rough textures. These results suggest that AR technology could enhance sweetness perception without increasing sugar, offering potential benefits for individuals controlling sugar intake. This approach also presents new design opportunities in the food industry by expanding AR's application in multisensory experiences.

articleTitle: Static Object Detection and Localization Technology Based on Multi Machine Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: In view of the problems of low detection efficiency, low accuracy and inaccurate target positioning of UAV static object, this paper proposes an object detection and localization technology based on multi-UAVS information fusion. Firstly, this paper designs a differentiated search algorithm for convex areas based on region segmentation for UAV formations, and conducts a coverage search of the target area. Secondly, the RT-DETR algorithm is improved, and its pre-processing and post-processing are modified. Finally, a target precise positioning algorithm based on K-means is proposed, which fuses the information of a single aircraft in the UAV formation. Experiments are carried out on the dataset constructed by the project team, and the results show that the proposed algorithm can greatly improve the accuracy and efficiency of object detection and positioning.

articleTitle: A Method for Ultra-Short-Term Wind Power Forecasting: Based on Parallel Transformer Encoder Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: To address the issue of low wind power prediction accuracy caused by the intermittent nature of wind power forecasting and the inability of the full connection layer in PatchTST and iTransformer to capture temporal correlations within tokens, an ultra-short-term wind power prediction model based on a parallel Transformer encoder is proposed. First, a time series convolution layer is introduced in PatchTST to extract the time series features of endogenous variables. Second, a cross-attention mechanism and a time series convolution layer are introduced in iTransformer to extract the time series features of exogenous variables. Finally, the extracted time series features of endogenous and exogenous variables are dimensionally aligned, and the final prediction results are output through Concatenate and BiLSTM. Through ablation studies and comparative experimental analyses, the proposed model demonstrates high accuracy and robustness in ultra-short-term wind power forecasting.

articleTitle: Detecting AI Generated Images Through Texture and Frequency Analysis of Patches
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: The significant improvement in AI image generation in recent years poses serious threats to social security, as AI generated misinformation may infringe upon political stability, personal privacy, and digital copy rights of artists. Building an AI generated image detector that accurately identifies generated image is crucial to maintain the social security and property rights of artists. This paper introduces preprocessing pipeline that uses positional encoded azimuthal integrals for image patches to create fingerprints that encapsulate distinguishing features. We then trained a multi-head attention model with 97.5% accuracy on classification of the fingerprints. The model also achieved 80% accuracy on images generated by AI models not presented in the training dataset, demonstrating the robustness of our pipeline and the potential of broader application of our model.

articleTitle: Automated Penetration Testing Based on MATD Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Artificial Intelligence, Virtual Reality and Visualization
abstract: With the rapid advancement of internet technology, cybersecurity risks are continuously increasing, and malicious cyberattacks have caused significant losses to users, making it crucial to maintain network security. Automated penetration testing plays a vital role in current cybersecurity efforts. However, existing automated penetration testing methods suffer from inefficiencies in information utilization, inaccurate action decision-making, and an overly large action space. To address these issues, we propose a new algorithm called Multi-Agent Task Decomposition(MATD), based on historical experience information and task decomposition. MATD enhances the efficiency of utilizing historical observation data through the use of Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) networks and reduces the action space of individual agents by employing a multi-task decomposition method. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms the traditional Proximal Policy Optimization(PPO) algorithm by achieving higher cumulative rewards in fewer steps, thereby improving decision-making in intelligent penetration testing. This approach holds promise for increasing the efficiency of penetration testing and enhancing overall network security.
